(education/starter repos omitted for brevity) —

Note: Topic-search repos without today's stars are shown with total stars only; trending repos carry today's delta.

Step 3: Report

1. Today's Highlights

The open-source AI ecosystem's center of gravity is unmistakably shifting toward agent-skill frameworks and agent-harness performance. Four of the top ten trending repos (mattpocock/skills, obra/superpowers, affaan-m/ECC, and ruvnet/ruflo) are entirely about codifying skills, instincts, and memory into reusable, cross-CLI agent harnesses — the "IDE for agents" moment is now. The explosive +3,362 stars for mattpocock/skills in a single day signals that the developer community is hungry for standardized, shareable agent skill packages rather than monolithic frameworks. Meanwhile, Apache Maka entering incubation as a local-first agent workspace underlines that auditability and append-only logs for agent activity are becoming first-class requirements. Finally, the presence of PostHog with AI-observability features in the trending list confirms that observability for agent-based products is moving from niche to mainstream.

2. Top Projects by Category

🔧 AI Infrastructure

  • PostHog/posthog — ⭐ (trending +335 today) — The leading self-driving-product platform now includes AI observability and MCP-based steering, making it the default choice for teams shipping agent-backed features.
  • modular/modular — ⭐ trending +913 today — The Modular Platform (MAX + Mojo) is gaining serious momentum as the high-performance, Pythonic alternative for AI inference and kernel development.
  • microsoft/onnxruntime — ⭐ trending +5 today — The cross-platform inference accelerator remains the bedrock for edge and cloud ML deployment; steady, unglamorous, and essential.
  • cursor/plugins — ⭐ trending +388 today — Cursor's official plugin spec is racing to become the de facto standard for editor-native agent extensions.
  • apache/maka — ⭐ trending +148 today — Apache Incubating local-first AI agent workspace with append-only logs for full auditability — a signal that enterprises are demanding verifiable agent trails.

🤖 AI Agents / Workflows

  • mattpocock/skills — ⭐ trending +3,362 today (🔥 top mover) — "Skills for Real Engineers" — a curated, battle-tested .agents directory that became the community's reference for agent skill engineering in one day.
  • obra/superpowers — ⭐ trending +790 today — An agentic skills framework plus a full software development methodology that "just works," sparking a wave of skill-first adoption.
  • affaan-m/ECC — ⭐ trending +357 today — Agent-harness performance optimization with skills, instincts, and memory — it hijacks your coding agents to make them better.
  • ruvnet/ruflo — ⭐ trending +140 today — The "original agent meta-harness" for multi-player swarms, adaptive memory, and RAG integration — it's becoming the backbone for autonomous multi-agent coordination.
  • shareAI-lab/learn-claude-code — ⭐ 74,903 total — The canonical "build a nano agent harness from scratch" tutorial; the pedagogical standard for agent internals.

📦 AI Applications

  • harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo — ⭐ trending +1,201 today — AI-driven HD short-video generation from a keyword — the most commercially pragmatic AI app of the day.
  • santifer/career-ops — ⭐ trending +921 today — Open-source AI job search with structured A–F rubric scoring of listings and auto CV tailoring — vertical AI done right.
  • CherryHQ/cherry-studio — ⭐ 50,887 total — AI productivity studio with 300+ assistants, unifying frontier LLMs into one local-first workspace.
  • siyuan-note/siyuan — ⭐ 45,920 total — Privacy-first knowledge workspace where human and AI agents co-edit — the "agent-native note" direction is here.

🧠 LLMs / Training

  • huggingface/transformers — ⭐ 164,317 total — The model-definition framework for state-of-the-art ML; still the beating heart of the open model ecosystem.
  • pytorch/pytorch — ⭐ 102,528 total — The dynamic neural network powerhouse dominating both research and production training.
  • elder-plinius/OBLITERATUS — ⭐ trending +63 today — Focused on jailbreak/alignment research; a niche but persistent signal of the continual cat-and-mouse in model safety.
  • Modular/Mojo — ⭐ trending +913 today — Also a training-adjacent language revival; Mojo's C-like speed with Python ergonomics is pulling ML engineers back to systems-level work.

🔍 RAG / Knowledge

  • langgenius/dify — ⭐ 153,147 total — The collaborative workspace for agentic workflows and RAG pipelines — still the fastest on-ramp from prototype to production.
  • infiniflow/ragflow — ⭐ 89,000 total — The leading open-source RAG engine fusing retrieval with deep agent capabilities for a superior context layer.
  • milvus-io/milvus — ⭐ 45,728 total — The cloud-native vector database that scales to billions of vectors; a must-have for enterprise RAG.
  • thedotmack/claude-mem — ⭐ 91,456 total — Persistent, compressed, cross-session agent memory — the missing link that turns stateless agents into long-term teammates.
  • headroomlabs-ai/headroom — ⭐ 67,122 total — Compresses tool outputs and RAG chunks by 60–95% before hitting the LLM — a token-economy breakthrough for cost-sensitive production agents.

3. Trend Signal Analysis

Three explosive signals dominate today's data. First, "Skills" are the new "Agents." The astronomical star velocity on mattpocock/skills and obra/superpowers is not incremental — it's a paradigm shift. The community has moved from building raw agents to cataloguing reusable, composable skill packages that any harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) can ingest. We're seeing the birth of a "skill package manager" concept before our eyes.

Second, agent-harness performance is a first-class engineering discipline. ECC, ruflo, and headroom are all attacking the same pain point: agents are token-hungry and context-starved. Whether through token compression (headroom, caveman's 65% token cut) or memory injection (claude-mem), developers are treating agent context windows like precious memory in an OS — and building virtual memory systems for AI. This is the "operating system for agents" layer.

Third, observability and auditability have arrived. Apache Maka's append-only agent logs and PostHog's AI observability suite signal that enterprises will not adopt autonomous agents at scale without traceable, replayable, and steerable execution trails. This is the missing enterprise credential that moves agents from demos to production.

Finally, vertical AI applications are proliferating. MoneyPrinterTurbo and career-ops show that small teams with one sharp use case and an LLM API can capture massive daily attention — the long tail of "AI-for-X" is minting hits daily.

4. Community Hot Spots

  • 🔥 mattpocock/skills — +3,362 stars in a day is a once-in-a-season event. If you build agents, you need to see how the industry's best engineer structures his .agents directory. This is the blueprint for your own skill library.
  • ⚡ obra/superpowers — A complete agentic development methodology in a repo. The "framework + philosophy" combo is what converts curious developers into daily agent users.
  • 🧠 thedotmack/claude-mem — The "persistent memory for every agent" problem is solved here. If you're tired of your agents forgetting everything between sessions, this is your fix — and it pairs with caveman for extreme token efficiency.
  • 💾 headroomlabs-ai/headroom — 60–95% token savings on JSON tool outputs is a production-cost game changer. In a world where API bills scale with token usage, this is the lowest-hanging fruit for CFO-friendly AI.
  • 🔍 infiniflow/ragflow — The RAG engine battle is not over; RAGFlow's fusion of retrieval with agent capabilities keeps it ahead of the pack. If you're architecting enterprise knowledge systems this week, it's still the favorite.
